Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
curated_comment: Wobzi Khroskyabs (guan1266, Trans-Himalayan, China) shows ergative alignment according to Lai (2017). The language is a well-documented Rgyalrong-type language of Sichuan. Ergative is present for 2nd/3rd person pronouns (GB409_3-4=1) but not 1st person (GB409_2=0), for full NPs (GB409_5=1), and consistently across all documented tense/aspect/mood/realis/clause-type contexts (GB409_6-14=1, GB409_16-22=1). GB409_15 (non-agentive A) remains '?' due to insufficient evidence in the source. GB409_23=0 (ergative ≠ genitive) and GB409_24=1 (ergative = instrumental). After PDF verification of Lai (2017), eight previously unresolved '?' values (GB409_9, 11, 13, 17, 19, 20, 21, 22) were resolved to 1; no conditioning splits found for these parameters. Glottocode guan1266 is correct; the previously proposed wobz1235 does not exist in Glottolog.
